summary: A small white wooden tower on the west pier at Port Dover, rebuilt in 1904-05 on the site of its predecessor and now owned by Norfolk County.

evidence.supports: old front range tower being taken down 1904
evidence.quote: The front range lighthouse, near the outer end of the west pier at Port Dover, Lake Erie, is being taken down, to be replaced by a new and improved tower.

evidence.supports: new tower built on site of old
evidence.quote: A front range lighthouse was built near the outer end of the west pier at Port Dover, on the site of the old lighthouse.
The tower is an inclosed wooden building, square in plan, with sloping sides, painted white, surmounted by a square iron lantern, painted red.
The light is a fixed white dioptric light, of the seventh order, elevated 34 feet above the level of the lake, and visible 11 miles from all points of approach by water.
This work was done by days
a lens lantern was hoisted atop a temporary pole erected fifty feet lakeward from the lighthouse

The design adopted for this lighthouse consists of a skeleton steel frame work surmounted by an inclosed wooden lantern, the whole painted red and 45 feet in height from the base to the vane on the lantern.

evidence.supports: rear light put in operation 11 June
evidence.quote: The light, which was put in operation on the 11th June last, is fixed red catoptric, elevated 45 feet above the lake level.

it was found necessary to establish a second light at Port Dover which, in range with the light on the outer end of the west breakwater pier would lead in to the railway wharf through the best channel.
